Please solve this issue: Our test suite grew big and we haven't noticed how the total RSpec run time outgrew 10 minutes (no parallelization) on CI.

We need to profile the test suite and identify the common problems (shared by many specs) and fix them once and for all. Keep refactoring of individual examples minimal: prefer configuration- and setup-level changes — adding tags, restructuring shared setup, wrapping execution. What the examples assert must stay the same. No app code changes affecting runtime behavior.

NOTE: Running the whole test suite is very time-consuming. Don't try to run the whole test suite (it would fail with timeout due to the Bash tool limitations) or even multiple directories. Only `rspec spec/<some-folder>`. Completely ignore system specs and streaming related specs (we do not run them by default anyway).

We will work on specific spec types at each optimization phase: `spec/models` and `spec/requests`. In the end, we want these two groups together to run at least twice as fast as they do today. Store any insights/comments/plans (such as baseline metrics) that could be useful for the future runs in the docs/ folder (so you can use that knowledge during future optimization runs).

Let's start with `spec/models`—don't touch other spec types during this step.
Also, do not touch factories yet — we will work on them later.

At least a 30-35% speed improvement for `spec/models` is expected; however, don't hesitate to squeeze more if you see an opportunity (aka low-hanging fruits).

## Overview

Before starting local development, read the [CONTRIBUTING] guide to understand
what changes are desirable and what general processes to use. You should also read the project's [AI Contribution Policy] to understand how we approach AI-assisted contributions.

## Environments

The following instructions will guide you through the process of setting up a local development instance of Mastodon on your computer.

There are instructions for these environments:

- [Vagrant](#vagrant)
- [macOS](#macos)
- [Linux](#linux)
- [Docker](#docker)
- [Dev Containers](#dev-containers)
- [GitHub Codespaces](#github-codespaces)

Once completed, continue with the [Next steps](#next-steps) section below.

### Vagrant

A **Vagrant** configuration is included for development purposes. To use it,
complete the following steps:

- Install Vagrant and Virtualbox
- Install the `vagrant-hostsupdater` plugin:
  `vagrant plugin install vagrant-hostsupdater`
- Run `vagrant up`
- Run `vagrant ssh -c "cd /vagrant && bin/dev"`
- Open `http://mastodon.local` in your browser

### macOS

To set up **macOS** for native development, complete the following steps:

- Install [Homebrew] and run:
  `brew install postgresql@14 redis libidn nvm vips`
  to install the required project dependencies
- Use a Ruby version manager to activate the ruby in `.ruby-version` and run
  `nvm use` to activate the node version from `.nvmrc`
- Start the database services by running `brew services start postgresql` and
  `brew services start redis`
- Run `RAILS_ENV=development bin/setup`, which will install the required ruby gems and node
  packages and prepare the database for local development

  (Note: If you are on Apple Silicon and get an error related to `libidn`, you should be able to fix this by running `gem install idn-ruby -- --with-idn-dir=$(brew --prefix libidn)`, then re-running the command above.)

- Finally, run the `bin/dev` script which will launch services via `overmind`
  (if installed) or `foreman`

### Linux

The Mastodon documentation has a [guide on installing Mastodon from source](https://docs.joinmastodon.org/dev/setup/#manual) on Linux.

### Docker

For production hosting and deployment with **Docker**, use the `Dockerfile` and
`docker-compose.yml` in the project root directory.

For local development, install and launch [Docker], and run:

```shell
docker compose -f .devcontainer/compose.yaml up -d
docker compose -f .devcontainer/compose.yaml exec app bin/setup
docker compose -f .devcontainer/compose.yaml exec app bin/dev
```

### Dev Containers

Within IDEs that support the [Development Containers] specification, start the
"Mastodon on local machine" container from the editor. The necessary `docker
compose` commands to build and setup the container should run automatically. For
**Visual Studio Code** this requires installing the [Dev Container extension].

### GitHub Codespaces

[GitHub Codespaces] provides a web-based version of VS Code and a cloud hosted
development environment configured with the software needed for this project.

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)][codespace]

- Click the button to create a new codespace, and confirm the options
- Wait for the environment to build (takes a few minutes)
- When the editor is ready, run `bin/dev` in the terminal
- Wait for an _Open in Browser_ prompt. This will open Mastodon
- On the _Ports_ tab "stream" setting change _Port visibility_ → _Public_

## Next steps

- Once you have successfully set up a development environment, it will be available on http://localhost:3000
- Log in as the default admin user with the username `admin@mastodon.local` or `admin@localhost` (depending on your setup) and the password `mastodonadmin`.
- Check out the [Mastodon docs] for tips on working with emails in development (you'll need this when creating new user accounts) as well as a list of useful commands for testing and updating your dev instance.
- You can optionally populate your database with sample data by running `bin/rails dev:populate_sample_data`. This will create a `@showcase_account` account with various types of contents.

require 'concurrent/atomic/cyclic_barrier'

module ThreadingHelpers
  def multi_threaded_execution(thread_count)
    barrier = Concurrent::CyclicBarrier.new(thread_count)

    threads = Array.new(thread_count) do |index|
      Thread.new do
        barrier.wait
        yield(index)
      end
    end

    threads.each(&:join)
  end
end

module DomainHelpers
  def configure_mx(domain:, exchange:, ip_v4_addr: '2.3.4.5', ip_v6_addr: 'fd00::2')
    resolver = instance_double(Resolv::DNS, :timeouts= => nil)

    allow(resolver).to receive(:getresources)
      .with(domain, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::MX)
      .and_return([double_mx(exchange)])
    allow(resolver)
      .to receive(:getresources)
      .with(domain, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::A)

    allow(resolver)

    allow(resolver)

    allow(resolver)

      .with(exchange, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::AAAA)
      .and_return([double_resource_v6(ip_v6_addr)])
    allow(Resolv::DNS)
      .to receive(:open)
      .and_yield(resolver)
  end

  def configure_dns(domain:, results:)
    resolver = instance_double(Resolv::DNS, :timeouts= => nil)

    allow(resolver).to receive(:getresources)
      .with(domain, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::MX)
      .and_return(results)
    allow(resolver)
      .to receive(:getresources)
      .with(domain, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::A)

      .with(domain, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::AAAA)
      .and_return(results)
    allow(Resolv::DNS)
      .to receive(:open)
      .and_yield(resolver)
  end

  def local_domain_uri
    Addressable::URI.parse("//#{Rails.configuration.x.local_domain}")

  def double_mx(exchange)
    instance_double(Resolv::DNS::Resource::MX, exchange: exchange)

    instance_double(Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::A, address: addr)

require 'concurrent/atomic/cyclic_barrier'

module ThreadingHelpers
  def multi_threaded_execution(thread_count)
    barrier = Concurrent::CyclicBarrier.new(thread_count)

    threads = Array.new(thread_count) do |index|
      Thread.new do
        barrier.wait
        yield(index)
      end
    end

    threads.each(&:join)
  end
end

module DomainHelpers
  def configure_mx(domain:, exchange:, ip_v4_addr: '2.3.4.5', ip_v6_addr: 'fd00::2')
    resolver = instance_double(Resolv::DNS, :timeouts= => nil)

    allow(resolver).to receive(:getresources)
      .with(domain, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::MX)
      .and_return([double_mx(exchange)])
    allow(resolver)
      .to receive(:getresources)
      .with(domain, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::A)
      .and_return([])
    allow(resolver)
      .to receive(:getresources)
      .with(domain, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::AAAA)
      .and_return([])
    allow(resolver)
      .to receive(:getresources)
      .with(exchange, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::A)
      .and_return([double_resource_v4(ip_v4_addr)])
    allow(resolver)
      .to receive(:getresources)
      .with(exchange, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::AAAA)
      .and_return([double_resource_v6(ip_v6_addr)])
    allow(Resolv::DNS)
      .to receive(:open)
      .and_yield(resolver)
  end

  def configure_dns(domain:, results:)
    resolver = instance_double(Resolv::DNS, :timeouts= => nil)

    allow(resolver).to receive(:getresources)
      .with(domain, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::MX)
      .and_return(results)
    allow(resolver)
      .to receive(:getresources)
      .with(domain, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::A)
      .and_return(results)
    allow(resolver)
      .to receive(:getresources)
      .with(domain, Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::AAAA)
      .and_return(results)
    allow(Resolv::DNS)
      .to receive(:open)
      .and_yield(resolver)
  end

  def local_domain_uri
    Addressable::URI.parse("//#{Rails.configuration.x.local_domain}")
  end

  private

  def double_mx(exchange)
    instance_double(Resolv::DNS::Resource::MX, exchange: exchange)
  end

  def double_resource_v4(addr)
    instance_double(Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::A, address: addr)
  end

  def double_resource_v6(addr)
    instance_double(Resolv::DNS::Resource::IN::AAAA, address: addr)
  end
end

messages.content: Local accounts call RSA-2048 keygen in `before_create`. Before deciding whether that matters, I want real numbers. I'll write a profiling helper outside the repo (in `tmp/perf/`) that does three things during a `spec/models` run: samples the stack with stackprof, times all SQL and its count, and counts/times RSA keygen calls. Then I'll run it in the background.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat .gitignore | grep -n "tmp\|log" ; mkdir -p tmp/perf && cat > tmp/perf/prof_helper.rb <<'EOF'
# Profiling helper (NOT part of repo). Loaded via: rspec --require ./tmp/perf/prof_helper.rb
require 'stackprof'

$perf = { sql_count: Hash.new(0), sql_time: Hash.new(0.0), rsa_count: 0, rsa_time: 0.0, examples: 0, sql_by_group: Hash.new(0) }

ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe('sql.active_record') do |*args|
  ev = ActiveSupport::Notifications::Event.new(*args)
  next if ev.payload[:cached] || ev.payload[:name] == 'SCHEMA'
  kind = ev.payload[:sql].to_s.split.first.to_s.upcase
  kind = ev.payload[:name] if ev.payload[:name].to_s.match?(/TRANSACTION|SAVEPOINT|RELEASE/i)
  $perf[:sql_count][kind] += 1
  $perf[:sql_time][kind] += ev.duration / 1000.0
end

module RSAProf
  def new(*args, **kw, &blk)
    return super unless args == [2048] && kw.empty?
    t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    r = super
    $perf[:rsa_time] += Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t
    $perf[:rsa_count] += 1
    r
  end
end
OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.singleton_class.prepend(RSAProf)

RSpec.configure do |c|
  c.before(:suite) { StackProf.start(mode: :wall, interval: 500, raw: true) }
  c.after(:suite) do
    StackProf.stop
    StackProf.results(ENV.fetch('PROF_OUT', 'tmp/perf/stack.dump'))
    File.write(ENV.fetch('PROF_OUT', 'tmp/perf/stack.dump') + '.stats.txt', [
      "SQL count by kind: #{$perf[:sql_count].sort_by { -_2 }.first(25).inspect}",
      "SQL time (ms) by kind: #{$perf[:sql_time].transform_values { _1.round(1) }.sort_by { -_2 }.first(25).inspect}",
      "total SQL time (ms): #{$perf[:sql_time].values.sum.round(1)}  total SQL count: #{$perf[:sql_count].values.sum}",
      "RSA(2048) keygen count: #{$perf[:rsa_count]}  total time: #{$perf[:rsa_time].round(2)}s",
    ].join("\n") + "\n")
  end
end
EOF
(nohup bash -c 'bundle exec rspec spec/models --seed 1234 --format progress --require ./tmp/perf/prof_helper.rb > tmp/perf/prof1.log 2>&1' >/dev/null 2>&1 &); echo started

    StackProf.start(mode: :wall, interval: 500, raw: true)
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe('sql.active_record') do |*args|
      ev = ActiveSupport::Notifications::Event.new(*args)
      next if ev.payload[:cached] || ev.payload[:name] == 'SCHEMA'
      kind = ev.payload[:sql].to_s.split.first.to_s.upcase
      kind = ev.payload[:name] if ev.payload[:name].to_s.match?(/TRANSACTION|SAVEPOINT|RELEASE/i)
      $perf[:sql_count][kind] += 1
      $perf[:sql_time][kind] += ev.duration / 1000.0
    end
  end
  c.after(:suite) do
    StackProf.stop
    out = ENV.fetch('PROF_OUT', 'tmp/perf/stack.dump')
    StackProf.results(out)
    File.write(out + '.stats.txt', [
      "SQL count by kind: #{$perf[:sql_count].sort_by { -_2 }.first(25).inspect}",
      "SQL time (ms) by kind: #{$perf[:sql_time].transform_values { _1.round(1) }.sort_by { -_2 }.first(25).inspect}",
      "total SQL time (ms): #{$perf[:sql_time].values.sum.round(1)}  total SQL count: #{$perf[:sql_count].values.sum}",
      "RSA(2048) keygen count: #{$perf[:rsa_count]}  total time: #{$perf[:rsa_time].round(2)}s",
    ].join("\n") + "\n")
  end
end

messages.content: That loop hit the tool timeout, because each `stackprof` call re-parses the large dump. I'll instead load the dump once in a small Ruby script and compute inclusive sample counts for each category in a single pass.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > tmp/perf/stack_cats.rb <<'EOF'
require 'stackprof'
data = Marshal.load(File.binread(ARGV[0]))
frames = data[:frames]
raw = data[:raw]
total = data[:samples]
pats = {
  'AR LogSubscriber#sql (SQL log formatting)' => /LogSubscriber#sql|LogSubscriber#log_query_source|LogSubscriber#/,
  'backtrace cleaner' => /BacktraceCleaner/,
  'PG exec (DB I/O)' => /PG::Connection/,
  'Fabrication gem' => /Fabrication|Fabricate/,
  'Fabricator/generators' => /Fabricator/,
  'BCrypt' => /BCrypt/,
  'Redis' => /Redis/,
  'Rails.cache / ActiveSupport::Cache' => /ActiveSupport::Cache/,
  'RSpec mocks' => /RSpec::Mocks|rspec-mocks|RSpec::Core/,
  'WebMock' => /WebMock/,
  'Sidekiq' => /Sidekiq/,
  'ActiveRecord::Callbacks' => /ActiveRecord::Callbacks|ActiveSupport::Callbacks/,
  'Validations' => /Validat/,
  'Associations' => /Association/,
  'Chewy' => /Chewy/,
  'Paperclip/vips' => /Paperclip|Vips|vips/i,
  'Nokogiri' => /Nokogiri/,
  'Devise' => /Devise/,
  'GC (sweeping/marking)' => /^\(sweeping\)|^\(marking\)/,
  'Transactions' => /Transaction/,
  'Setting/Settings' => /Setting/,
}
incl = Hash.new(0)
self_c = Hash.new(0)
i = 0
samples = 0
while i < raw.size
  len = raw[i]; stack = raw[i+1, len]; count = raw[i+1+len]
  i += len + 2
  samples += count
  names = stack.map { |fid| frames[fid][:name].to_s }
  pats.each do |label, rx|
    incl[label] += count if names.any? { _1.match?(rx) }
  end
  self_c[frames[stack.first][:name].to_s] += count
end
puts "total samples #{samples} (report says #{total})"
pats.each { |l, _| printf("%6.1f%%  %s\n", incl[l] * 100.0 / samples, l) }
EOF
timeout 200 bundle exec ruby tmp/perf/stack_cats.rb tmp/perf/stack.dump 2>&1 | tail -30

# Exclusive attribution: walk leaf -> root, assign sample to first matching category.
# NOTE: raw stacks are root-first, so the leaf is stack.last.
require 'stackprof'
data = Marshal.load(File.binread(ARGV[0]))
frames = data[:frames]; raw = data[:raw]
cats = [
  ['SQL log formatting (AR LogSubscriber + BacktraceCleaner)', /LogSubscriber|BacktraceCleaner|each_caller_location|Backtrace::Location/],
  ['DB I/O (PG::Connection)', /PG::Connection/],
  ['Redis I/O (RedisClient / redis-rb)', /Redis/],
  ['Sidekiq plumbing', /Sidekiq/],
  ['Fabrication (factories)', /Fabricat/],
  ['RSpec mocks/stubs', /RSpec::Mocks|rspec-mocks/],
  ['BCrypt', /BCrypt/],
  ['WebMock/HTTP', /WebMock|Net::HTTP/],
  ['Chewy', /Chewy/],
  ['Paperclip/vips/ffmpeg', /Paperclip|Vips|vips/i],
  ['GC', /^\(sweeping\)|^\(marking\)|^\(garbage/],
  ['ActiveSupport::Cache', /ActiveSupport::Cache/],
  ['Arel/SQL building', /Arel/],
  ['ActiveRecord/ActiveModel (framework)', /ActiveRecord|ActiveModel|ActiveSupport::Callbacks/],
  ['Rails other / ActiveSupport', /Rails|ActiveSupport|ActionMailer/],
  ['RSpec (runner/other)', /RSpec/],
  ['Idle wait (IO.select / read)', /IO\.select|wait_readable|IO#read/],
]
excl = Hash.new(0); samples = 0; i = 0
redis_sites = Hash.new(0)
app_sites = Hash.new(0)
while i < raw.size
  len = raw[i]; stack = raw[i+1, len]; count = raw[i+1+len]; i += len + 2
  samples += count
  leaf_first = stack.reverse
  hit = nil
  leaf_first.each do |fid|
    f = frames[fid]; n = f[:name].to_s; file = f[:file].to_s
    cat = cats.find { |_, rx| n.match?(rx) }
    if cat then hit = cat[0]; break end
    if file.start_with?('/app/') then hit = 'Application code (app/ lib/ spec/)'; app_sites["#{n} #{file.sub('/app/','')}:#{f[:line]}"] += count; break end
  end
  hit ||= 'other (gems)'
  excl[hit] += count
  if hit.start_with?('Redis')
    site = leaf_first.map { frames[_1] }.find { |f| f[:name].to_s !~ /Redis/ && f[:file].to_s !~ /redis/ }
    redis_sites["#{site[:name]} #{site[:file].to_s.sub('/app/','').sub(%r{.*/gems/},'')}:#{site[:line]}"] += count if site
  end
end
puts "samples #{samples}"
excl.sort_by { -_2 }.each { |k, v| printf("%6.1f%%  %s\n", v * 100.0 / samples, k) }
puts "\nTop Redis call sites (first non-redis frame, leaf-first):"
redis_sites.sort_by { -_2 }.first(10).each { |k, v| printf("%6.1f%%  %s\n", v * 100.0 / samples, k) }
puts "\nTop app-code self-sites:"
app_sites.sort_by { -_2 }.first(25).each { |k, v| printf("%6.2f%%  %s\n", v * 100.0 / samples, k) }
EOF

messages.content:
Now the leaf-level picture is clearer:

- DB round trips (PG exec calls) about 16%
- GC about 4.5%
- BCrypt about 1.5%
- The rest is spread thin across ActiveRecord/ActiveSupport internals, which is what you'd expect from record-heavy specs

Since DB round trips and record creation are what's left, I want to know where the ~113k queries (about 63 per example) come from. I'll profile query sources: per spec file, most frequent normalized SQL, and the first app-code call site. That shows whether repeated lookups (e.g. settings or roles) or heavy `before` blocks are responsible.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > tmp/perf/sql_helper.rb <<'EOF'
# SQL source profiling helper (NOT part of repo).
$sqlp = { by_file: Hash.new(0), by_stmt: Hash.new(0), by_site: Hash.new(0), by_example: Hash.new(0), total: 0 }
RSpec.configure do |c|
  c.before(:suite) do
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe('sql.active_record') do |*args|
      ev = ActiveSupport::Notifications::Event.new(*args)
      p = ev.payload
      next if p[:cached] || p[:name] == 'SCHEMA'
      $sqlp[:total] += 1
      ex = RSpec.current_example
      file = ex ? ex.metadata[:file_path] : '(no example)'
      $sqlp[:by_file][file] += 1
      $sqlp[:by_example][ex ? ex.full_description[0, 140] : '(none)'] += 1
      norm = p[:sql].to_s.gsub(/\$\d+/, '?').gsub(/\b\d+\b/, 'N').gsub(/'[^']*'/, "'S'").gsub(/\s+/, ' ')[0, 220]
      $sqlp[:by_stmt][norm] += 1
      site = caller_locations(1, 60).find { |l| l.path.start_with?('/app/app/', '/app/lib/', '/app/spec/fabricators', '/app/spec/support') }
      $sqlp[:by_site]["#{site.path.sub('/app/', '')}:#{site.lineno} #{site.label[0,60]}"] += 1 if site
    end
  end
  c.after(:suite) do
    File.write('tmp/perf/sql_profile.txt', [
      "TOTAL #{$sqlp[:total]}",
      "== by file", *$sqlp[:by_file].sort_by { -_2 }.first(40).map { |k, v| format('%7d %s', v, k) },
      "== by statement", *$sqlp[:by_stmt].sort_by { -_2 }.first(60).map { |k, v| format('%7d %s', v, k) },
      "== by first app call site", *$sqlp[:by_site].sort_by { -_2 }.first(60).map { |k, v| format('%7d %s', v, k) },
      "== by example (top)", *$sqlp[:by_example].sort_by { -_2 }.first(30).map { |k, v| format('%7d %s', v, k) },
    ].join("\n") + "\n")
  end
end
EOF
(nohup bash -c 'bundle exec rspec spec/models --seed 1234 --format progress --require ./tmp/perf/sql_helper.rb > tmp/perf/sql1.log 2>&1' >/dev/null 2>&1 &); echo started

# frozen_string_literal: true

module TestProf
  module BeforeAll
    module Adapters
      # ActiveRecord adapter for `before_all`
      module ActiveRecord
        POOL_ARGS = ((::ActiveRecord::VERSION::MAJOR > 6) ? [:writing] : []).freeze

        class << self
          if ::ActiveRecord::Base.connection.pool.respond_to?(:pin_connection!)
            def begin_transaction
              subscribe!
              ::ActiveRecord::Base.connection_handler.connection_pool_list(:writing).each do |pool|
                pool.pin_connection!(true)
              end
            end

            def rollback_transaction
              ::ActiveRecord::Base.connection_handler.connection_pool_list(:writing).each do |pool|
                pool.unpin_connection!
              end
              unsubscribe!
            end

            def subscribe!
              Thread.current[:before_all_subscription_count] ||= 0
              Thread.current[:before_all_subscription_count] += 1

              return unless Thread.current[:before_all_subscription_count] == 1

              Thread.current[:before_all_connection_subscriber] = ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe("!connection.active_record") do |_, _, _, _, payload|
                connection_name = payload[:connection_name] if payload.key?(:connection_name)
                shard = payload[:shard] if payload.key?(:shard)
                next unless connection_name

                pool = ::ActiveRecord::Base.connection_handler.retrieve_connection_pool(connection_name, shard: shard)
                next unless pool && pool.role == :writing

                pool.pin_connection!(true)
              end
            end

            def unsubscribe!
              return unless Thread.current[:before_all_subscription_count]

              Thread.current[:before_all_subscription_count] -= 1

              return unless Thread.current[:before_all_subscription_count] == 0 && Thread.current[:before_all_connection_subscriber]

              ActiveSupport::Notifications.unsubscribe(Thread.current[:before_all_connection_subscriber])
              Thread.current[:before_all_connection_subscriber] = nil
            end
          else

  # NOTE: Experimental and magical, for more control use `before_all`.
  module LetItBe
    class DuplicationError < StandardError; end

    Modifier = Struct.new(:scope, :block) do
      def call(record, config)
        block.call(record, config)
      end
    end

    class Configuration
      attr_accessor :report_duplicates

      # Define an alias for `let_it_be` with the predefined options:
      #
      #   TestProf::LetItBe.configure do |config|
      #     config.alias_to :let_it_be_reloaded, reload: true
      #   end
      def alias_to(name, **default_args)
        LetItBe.define_let_it_be_alias(name, **default_args)
      end

      # Register modifier by providing the name of key,
      # optional scope (when to apply the modifier, on initialization (:initialize)
      # or when accessed # via let (:let))
      def register_modifier(key, on: :let, &block)
        raise ArgumentError, "Modifier #{key} is already defined for let_it_be" if LetItBe.modifiers.key?(key)

        LetItBe.modifiers[key] = Modifier.new(on, block)
      end

      def default_modifiers
        @default_modifiers ||= {}
      end
    end

    class << self
      def config
        @config ||= Configuration.new
      end

      def configure
        yield config
      end

      def modifiers
        @modifiers ||= {}
      end

      def wrap_with_modifiers(mods, on: :let, &block)
        mods = mods.select { |k, val| LetItBe.modifiers.fetch(k).scope == on }
        return block if mods.empty?

        validate_modifiers! mods

        proc do
          record = instance_eval(&block)
          mods.inject(record) do |rec, (k, v)|
            LetItBe.modifiers.fetch(k).call(rec, v)
          end
        end
      end

      def module_for(group)
        modules[group] ||= Module.new.tap { |mod| group.prepend(mod) }
      end

      private

      def modules
        @modules ||= {}
      end

      def validate_modifiers!(mods)
        unknown = mods.keys - modifiers.keys
        return if unknown.empty?

        raise ArgumentError, "Unknown let_it_be modifiers were used: #{unknown.join(", ")}. " \
                             "Available modifiers are: #{modifiers.keys.join(", ")}"
      end
    end

    # Use uniq prefix for instance variables to avoid collisions
    # We want to use the power of Ruby's unicode support)
    # And we love cats!)
    # Allow overriding the prefix (there are some intermittent issues on JRuby still)
    PREFIX = ENV.fetch("LET_IT_BE_IVAR_PREFIX", "@😸")

    def self.define_let_it_be_alias(name, **default_args)
      define_method(name) do |identifier, **options, &blk|
        let_it_be(identifier, **default_args.merge(options), &blk)
      end
    end

    def let_it_be(identifier, **options, &block)
      initializer = proc do
        instance_variable_set(:"#{TestProf::LetItBe::PREFIX}#{identifier}", instance_exec(&block))
      rescue FrozenError => e
        raise e.exception("#{e.message}#{TestProf::LetItBe::FROZEN_ERROR_HINT}")
      end

      default_options = LetItBe.config.default_modifiers.dup
      default_options.merge!(metadata[:let_it_be_modifiers]) if metadata[:let_it_be_modifiers]

      options = default_options.merge(options)

      initializer = LetItBe.wrap_with_modifiers(options, on: :initialize, &initializer)

      before_all(&initializer)

      let_accessor = LetItBe.wrap_with_modifiers(options, on: :let) do
        instance_variable_get(:"#{PREFIX}#{identifier}")
      end

      report_duplicates(identifier) if LetItBe.config.report_duplicates

      LetItBe.module_for(self).module_eval do
        define_method(identifier) do
          # Trying to detect the context
          # First, check for ::RSpec.current_scope (modern RSpec) and then read @__inspect_output
          # (based on https://github.com/rspec/rspec-rails/commit/7cb796db064f58da7790a92e73ab906ef50b1f34)
          if ::RSpec.respond_to?(:current_scope) && %i[before_all before_context_hook after_context_hook].include?(::RSpec.current_scope)
            instance_variable_get(:"#{PREFIX}#{identifier}")
          elsif /(before|after)\(:context\)/.match?(@__inspect_output) || @__inspect_output.include?("before_all")
            instance_variable_get(:"#{PREFIX}#{identifier}")
          else
            super()
          end
        end
      end

      let(identifier, &let_accessor)
    end

    private def report_duplicates(identifier)
      if method_defined?(identifier) && File.basename(__FILE__) == File.basename(instance_method(identifier).source_location[0])
        error_msg = "let_it_be(:#{identifier}) was redefined in nested group"
        report_level = LetItBe.config.report_duplicates.to_sym

        if report_level == :warn
          ::RSpec.warn_with(error_msg)

# frozen_string_literal: true

# Profiling helper for RSpec runs. NOT loaded by default; opt in with:
#
#   PROF_OUT=tmp/perf/stack.dump bundle exec rspec spec/models \
#     --require ./docs/test-performance/tools/prof_helper.rb
#
# Produces:
#   * a StackProf wall-mode dump (analyse with stack_excl.rb / stack_self.rb)
#   * a stats file (<dump>.stats.txt) with SQL counts/time per statement kind and
#     the RSA(2048) keygen count/time.
#
# Overhead: StackProf adds ~10-20% wall time; compare relative shares, not absolutes.

require 'stackprof'
require 'openssl'

$perf = { sql_count: Hash.new(0), sql_time: Hash.new(0.0), rsa_count: 0, rsa_time: 0.0 }

module RSAProf
  def new(*args, **kw, &blk)
    return super unless args == [2048] && kw.empty?

    t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    r = super
    $perf[:rsa_time] += Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t
    $perf[:rsa_count] += 1
    r
  end
end
OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.singleton_class.prepend(RSAProf)

RSpec.configure do |c|
  c.before(:suite) do
    StackProf.start(mode: :wall, interval: 500, raw: true)
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe('sql.active_record') do |*args|
      ev = ActiveSupport::Notifications::Event.new(*args)
      next if ev.payload[:cached] || ev.payload[:name] == 'SCHEMA'

      kind = ev.payload[:sql].to_s.split.first.to_s.upcase
      kind = ev.payload[:name] if ev.payload[:name].to_s.match?(/TRANSACTION|SAVEPOINT|RELEASE/i)
      $perf[:sql_count][kind] += 1
      # ActiveSupport event durations are already in milliseconds.
      $perf[:sql_time][kind] += ev.duration
    end
  end

  c.after(:suite) do
    StackProf.stop
    out = ENV.fetch('PROF_OUT', 'tmp/perf/stack.dump')
    StackProf.results(out)
    File.write(
      "#{out}.stats.txt",
      [
        "SQL count by kind: #{$perf[:sql_count].sort_by { -_2 }.first(25).inspect}",
        "SQL time (ms) by kind: #{$perf[:sql_time].transform_values { _1.round(1) }.sort_by { -_2 }.first(25).inspect}",
        "total SQL time (ms): #{$perf[:sql_time].values.sum.round(1)}  total SQL count: #{$perf[:sql_count].values.sum}",
        "RSA(2048) keygen count: #{$perf[:rsa_count]}  total time: #{$perf[:rsa_time].round(2)}s",
      ].join("\n") + "\n"
    )
  end
end
EOF
cat > stack_excl.rb <<'EOF'
# frozen_string_literal: true

# Exclusive (leaf-first) attribution of a StackProf raw dump to cost categories.
#
#   bundle exec ruby docs/test-performance/tools/stack_excl.rb tmp/perf/stack.dump
#
# IMPORTANT: StackProf raw stacks are stored ROOT-FIRST, so the leaf is `stack.last`.
# Each sample is assigned to the innermost frame that matches a category; app code is
# recognised by the /app/ path prefix (gem paths also contain "lib/", so don't match that).

require 'stackprof'

data = Marshal.load(File.binread(ARGV[0]))
frames = data[:frames]
raw = data[:raw]

CATEGORIES = [
  ['SQL log formatting (AR LogSubscriber + BacktraceCleaner)', /LogSubscriber|BacktraceCleaner|each_caller_location|Backtrace::Location/],
  ['DB I/O (PG::Connection)', /PG::Connection/],
  ['Redis I/O', /Redis/],
  ['Sidekiq plumbing', /Sidekiq/],
  ['Fabrication (factories)', /Fabricat/],
  ['RSpec mocks/stubs', /RSpec::Mocks|rspec-mocks/],
  ['BCrypt', /BCrypt/],
  ['WebMock/HTTP', /WebMock|Net::HTTP/],
  ['Chewy', /Chewy/],
  ['Paperclip/vips/ffmpeg', /Paperclip|Vips|vips/i],
  ['GC', /^\(sweeping\)|^\(marking\)|^\(garbage/],
  ['ActiveSupport::Cache', /ActiveSupport::Cache/],
  ['Arel/SQL building', /Arel/],
  ['ActiveRecord/ActiveModel (framework)', /ActiveRecord|ActiveModel|ActiveSupport::Callbacks/],
  ['Rails other / ActiveSupport', /Rails|ActiveSupport|ActionMailer/],
  ['RSpec (runner/other)', /RSpec/],
  ['Idle wait (IO.select / read)', /IO\.select|wait_readable|IO#read/],
].freeze

excl = Hash.new(0)
app_sites = Hash.new(0)
samples = 0
i = 0
while i < raw.size
  len = raw[i]
  stack = raw[i + 1, len]
  count = raw[i + 1 + len]
  i += len + 2
  samples += count

  hit = nil
  stack.reverse_each do |fid|
    f = frames[fid]
    name = f[:name].to_s
    cat = CATEGORIES.find { |_, rx| name.match?(rx) }
    if cat
      hit = cat[0]
      break
    end
    next unless f[:file].to_s.start_with?('/app/')

    hit = 'Application code (app/ lib/ spec/)'
    app_sites["#{name} #{f[:file].sub('/app/', '')}:#{f[:line]}"] += count
    break
  end
  excl[hit || 'other (gems)'] += count
end

puts "samples #{samples}"
excl.sort_by { -_2 }.each { |k, v| printf("%6.1f%%  %s\n", v * 100.0 / samples, k) }
puts "\nTop app-code leaf frames:"
app_sites.sort_by { -_2 }.first(20).each { |k, v| printf("%6.2f%%  %s\n", v * 100.0 / samples, k) }
EOF
cat > stack_self.rb <<'EOF'
# frozen_string_literal: true

# Top leaf (self-time) frames of a StackProf raw dump.
#
#   bundle exec ruby docs/test-performance/tools/stack_self.rb tmp/perf/stack.dump [limit]
#
# Raw stacks are root-first, so the leaf is `stack.last`.

require 'stackprof'

data = Marshal.load(File.binread(ARGV[0]))
frames = data[:frames]
raw = data[:raw]
limit = (ARGV[1] || 40).to_i

total = 0
selfc = Hash.new(0)
i = 0
while i < raw.size
  len = raw[i]
  stack = raw[i + 1, len]
  count = raw[i + 1 + len]
  i += len + 2
  total += count
  leaf = frames[stack.last]
  file = leaf[:file].to_s.sub(%r{.*/gems/}, '').sub('/app/', '')
  selfc["#{leaf[:name]}  (#{file}:#{leaf[:line]})"] += count
end

puts "samples #{total}"
selfc.sort_by { -_2 }.first(limit).each { |k, v| printf("%6.2f%%  %s\n", v * 100.0 / total, k) }
EOF
cat > sql_helper.rb <<'EOF'
# frozen_string_literal: true

# SQL source profiler (NOT loaded by default). Groups executed SQL by spec file,
# by normalised statement, by first app call site and by example.
#
#   bundle exec rspec spec/models --require ./docs/test-performance/tools/sql_helper.rb
#   -> writes tmp/perf/sql_profile.txt
#
# Note: this adds overhead (caller_locations per query); use it for counts, not timings.

$sqlp = { by_file: Hash.new(0), by_stmt: Hash.new(0), by_site: Hash.new(0), by_example: Hash.new(0), total: 0 }

RSpec.configure do |c|
  c.before(:suite) do
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe('sql.active_record') do |*args|
      ev = ActiveSupport::Notifications::Event.new(*args)
      p = ev.payload
      next if p[:cached] || p[:name] == 'SCHEMA'

      $sqlp[:total] += 1
      ex = RSpec.current_example
      $sqlp[:by_file][ex ? ex.metadata[:file_path] : '(no example)'] += 1
      $sqlp[:by_example][ex ? ex.full_description[0, 140] : '(none)'] += 1
      norm = p[:sql].to_s.gsub(/\$\d+/, '?').gsub(/\b\d+\b/, 'N').gsub(/'[^']*'/, "'S'").gsub(/\s+/, ' ')[0, 220]
      $sqlp[:by_stmt][norm] += 1
      site = caller_locations(1, 60).find { |l| l.path.start_with?('/app/app/', '/app/lib/', '/app/spec/fabricators', '/app/spec/support') }
      $sqlp[:by_site]["#{site.path.sub('/app/', '')}:#{site.lineno} #{site.label[0, 60]}"] += 1 if site
    end
  end

  c.after(:suite) do
    File.write(
      'tmp/perf/sql_profile.txt',
      [
        "TOTAL #{$sqlp[:total]}",
        '== by file', *$sqlp[:by_file].sort_by { -_2 }.first(40).map { |k, v| format('%7d %s', v, k) },
        '== by statement', *$sqlp[:by_stmt].sort_by { -_2 }.first(60).map { |k, v| format('%7d %s', v, k) },
        '== by first app call site', *$sqlp[:by_site].sort_by { -_2 }.first(60).map { |k, v| format('%7d %s', v, k) },
        '== by example (top)', *$sqlp[:by_example].sort_by { -_2 }.first(30).map { |k, v| format('%7d %s', v, k) },
      ].join("\n") + "\n"
    )
  end
end
EOF
